items.summary: AGI - Api, falene e altri insetti impollinatori ,   in presenza di aria inquinata, hanno grandi difficoltà nell'individuare i fiori con l'olfatto. Lo afferma una ricerca condotta dall' Università di Reading.  Gli scienziati hanno analizzato 22 studi sperimentali su come gli inquinanti atmosferici ozono e ossidi di azoto (NOx) influenzano gli impollinatori. Entrambi gli inquinanti rendono più difficile per gli impollinatori trovare i fiori, degradando o alterando i profumi che questi emanano. L'impatto di ozono e ossidi di azoto La nuova ricerca, pubblicata sulla rivista Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment , ha rilevato che l'aumento dell'ozono ha ridotto le prestazioni degli impollinatori in media del 42% , mentre gli ossidi di azoto (NOx) le hanno ridotte del 46% . Quando i due inquinanti erano presenti contemporaneamente, la riduzione media era del 68% . Solo pochi studi hanno testato entrambi gli inquinanti insieme e, in questi, il danno aggiuntivo derivante dalla loro combinazione era inferiore a quanto suggerito dalle medie. items.title: ‘Like a drill going into my eye’: why the mystery over Havana syndrome refuses to die
items.summary: Dozens of CIA officers have been afflicted by debilitating symptoms over the past decade. Are they the result of ‘mass hysteria’? Or are they from attacks with an energy weapon and, if so, who is responsible? And has there been a cover-up? Shortly after 1am one night in April 2019, a CIA officer on a work trip to London was jolted awake in his hotel room by the most intense head pain he had ever experienced. His body was soaked with sweat and he felt like his eyes were spinning in their sockets. He manoeuvred his way out of bed, hoping to make it to the bathroom to vomit, but found his sense of balance had deserted him. Eventually, he fell back into a fitful, shallow sleep. The next day, arriving at the work meeting he had travelled for, the officer found he could not remember the names of colleagues in the room, people he knew well. As the meeting got under way, he could barely follow the discussion. Initially, he chalked it up to a terrible – if rather odd – case of food poisoning. But over subsequent weeks, worrying symptoms persisted: brain fog, loss of balance and increasingly harsh tinnitus. Continue reading...
